input.question: If one is lactose intolerant and they regularly consume lactose free milk, is this still potentially bad for them?
input.ground_truth: Lactose is a disaccharide sugar made of a bound glucose and galactose. During digestion, lactose gets broken up into these two constituents. Generally, someone who is lactose intolerant is simply lacking an enzyme called lactase that breaks that bond. Someone who is *lactose tolerant* is not utilizing intact molecules of lactose anyway. Therefore I can't see any negative effects of cutting out lactose from the diet. Lactose free milk has simply been "predigested" to cleave the lactose into glucose and galactose.

Okay! Imagine you have a tummy that doesn't like milk sugar (that's called lactose). So, you drink special milk that doesn't have that sugar in it—this is called lactose-free milk.

Now, is drinking this special milk always good for you? Well, usually it's fine! This milk is made so your tummy won't hurt. But… if you drink too much of anything—even special milk—it might not be the best for you. Too much of anything can make you gain weight or get too much of some things your body doesn't need a lot of.

Also, sometimes the special milk has a little bit of sugar or other stuff in it to make it taste good. If you drink a lot of that, too much sugar can be not so good for your teeth or your body.

So, drinking lactose-free milk is usually okay for you if you are lactose intolerant! But, like with anything, too much of anything is not always good. It's best to have it as part of a balanced diet with lots of different healthy foods.
